_README: Fifth held-out set, written 2026-10-04 BEFORE any pipeline dev result for the change it certifies: pooling an IPC definition's retrieval ranks with its punishing section's (`pair`, src/retrieval/ranker.pool_pairs). Held-out 3 #10 and held-out 4 #7 (threats to kill charged as attempt to murder) were spent finding it.

Weighted to the IPC, the only code `pair` changes: offences split into a definition and a punishment (intimidation 503/506, house-trespass 442/448, extortion 383/384, wrongful restraint 339/341, criminal breach of trust 405/406, mischief 425/426, kidnapping 359/363, hurt 321/323, defamation 499/500, theft 378/379). Case 2 is a REAL attempt to murder, to catch the opposite error (a blow that missed read as a mere threat). Cases 11-12 are BNS checks; 14-15 are purely civil controls, ungated.
HELD OUT. Committed before any run. Score once with scripts/eval_broad.py and re-score with scripts/score_runs.py. Never tune on it.

Synthetic facts. Section ids checked against the ingested statutes by scripts/check_fixture_ids.py; `relevant` is Claude's legal call, NOT reviewed by a lawyer. `arguable` sections are not counted against the pipeline.

cases.query: The complainant had filed a police complaint about the accused's illegal sand mining. The accused came to his house at night and told him, in front of his wife, that if the complaint was not withdrawn within a week he would be killed and his house burnt down. He then left.

During a fight over a drain, the accused shouted that he would finish the complainant and swung an axe at his head with full force. The complainant ducked; the axe struck the door frame behind him and split it. Neighbours then disarmed the accused.

After a quarrel about a water tap, the accused walked into the complainant's house through the open front door without permission while only the elderly mother was at home, shouted abuse at her for several minutes in the kitchen and left.

For five months the accused collected two thousand rupees every Saturday from the complainant, a vegetable seller, telling him that if he stopped paying his cart would be overturned and his stall would not be allowed in the market. The complainant paid out of fear.

As the complainant, a nurse, walked to the hospital for her night shift, the accused and his cousin stood across the narrow lane and would not let her pass for about twenty minutes, stepping in front of her each time she tried to go round them.

Before going abroad for a year, the complainant left her gold jewellery with the accused, a family friend, for safekeeping. When she returned and asked for it, he said he had pledged it with a moneylender to pay his own debts and could not give it back.

Angry that the complainant had refused to sell him a strip of land, the accused deliberately drove his tractor back and forth through the complainant's standing sugarcane, flattening about an acre of the crop.

The accused, a 24-year-old man, persuaded the complainant's fifteen-year-old daughter to leave her parents' home at night, promising to marry her, and took her by bus to another town. Her parents had not consented.

When the complainant objected to the accused parking his car in front of his gate, the accused slapped him twice and punched him in the face, leaving a swelling under his eye. The doctor recorded the injury as simple.

The accused posted in the housing society's WhatsApp group of about three hundred members that the complainant, the society's treasurer, had been jailed for fraud in his previous job. The complainant has never been charged with any offence, and the accused had no basis for the claim.

During divorce proceedings, the complainant's husband phoned her and said that unless she withdrew her maintenance case he would have her brother killed. He repeated the threat in a voice message the next day.
Two men on a motorcycle rode up behind the complainant as she walked home, and the pillion rider pulled the gold chain from her neck before they sped away.

At about two in the morning, while the family slept, the accused climbed in through an open bedroom window of the complainant's house and took a mobile phone and twelve thousand rupees in cash from the bedside table.

When the tenant moved out, the landlord kept twenty thousand rupees of the security deposit for repainting, saying the walls were damaged. The tenant says the marks were ordinary wear and wants the full deposit back.
A building contractor finished the owner's house four months after the date in the contract because of a shortage of cement. The owner wants a reduction in the final payment for the delay.
